_about: Utah lawn-conversion incentives. One saved table, not live lookups. Rates and caps change; each row carries last_checked and verified. Rates in USD per sq ft of lawn removed. 'estimated up to' uses rate_high. Sources are the Utah Water Savers portal and provider pages where reachable; rows marked verified=false were compiled from secondary summaries and must be confirmed on utahwatersavers.com before the pitch.

statewide_rules.program: Utah Water Savers Landscape Incentive Program (Utah Division of Water Resources + local providers)
statewide_rules.virtual_inspection_allowed: Utah Admin Code R653-11-7 allows completion inspections to be physical or virtual
disqualifiers: Removing or killing lawn before approval
Lawn not living and maintained at application
Account not in good standing with water provider
City without a qualifying water-efficient landscape ordinance
statewide_rules.legal: Utah Code 73-10-34 (2022 H.B. 121 turf removal incentive); Utah Admin Code R653-11

providers.name: Jordan Valley Water Conservancy District (member cities)
providers.notes: Rate depends on the member city's own match; $3.00 reported for JVWCD-direct customers. Localscapes plan required.

providers.name: Salt Lake City Department of Public Utilities
providers.notes: Salt Lake City adopted a qualifying landscape ordinance (listed among eligible municipalities in 2023). SLCDPU has also run its own Landscape Leadership Grant. Exact 2026 rate for SLCDPU customers not confirmed from a primary source.

providers.name: Central Utah Water Conservancy District (member cities)
Utah Division of Water Resources statewide track
providers.notes: Fallback for addresses in a city with a qualifying ordinance but no local program. Rate reported at $1/sq ft; confirm.
